Finite claim categories are independent of retrieval or rendering logic; unknown serialized categories use the parser fallback.
Reads serialized enum values with a conservative milestone fallback; direct Enum instances are not the JSON input contract.
Lifecycle labels separate active, superseded, contested and background claims without implying evidence verification.

Keeps supporting, contradicting and updating roles in separate collections; these roles are not collapsed during serialization.
Returns a new concatenated list so consumer list edits cannot remove records from role collections.
Considers all three evidence roles, including evidence that only contradicts a claim.
Preserves role separation, verification summary and source coverage for later audit/projections.
Rebuilds each role independently and sanitizes mapping-shaped summaries through the shared local coercion helper.
Skips non-dict members while preserving order; item parsing is delegated to EvidenceArticle rather than duplicated.
Mutable build-time claim record keeps provenance, confidence and evidence separate; persisted revision ownership belongs to the store.

Only explicit background lifecycle status exempts evidence; contested/superseded entries still need support provenance.

Records redundant membership for auditing; branch assignment conflicts are resolved by occurrence-aware reconciliation.
Copies membership/tag lists and preserves parent link, confidence and descriptive context.

Preserves original retrieval/pipeline/artifact inputs as provenance, independent of resulting projections.

Preserves status and supporting details without recalculating the finding during export.

Selects the worst of the known severity order; callers construct known statuses or use the deserializer normalization.
Includes both warning and failure messages while excluding passed checks.
Calculates counts from findings at export time, keeping severity totals aligned with the aggregate status.
Rebuilds findings only from mapping records and normalizes their severity through the finding parser.
Clarified mutable build-time versus immutable persisted revision semantics; schema version and provenance remain explicit.

Ignores unparseable entry dates and returns None when no valid years exist; no invented temporal coverage.
First-record deduplication preserves evidence order and now distinguishes long titles through the corrected evidence ID.
Exports the complete revision contract from entries/branches/graph/audit and input scope, not from a projection.
Rejects unsupported/missing schema versions before deserializing; skips nonrecord list members and leaves semantic integrity checks to audit.
Occurrence-indexed immutable results preserve duplicated IDs without collapsing evidence during repair.

Reviewed duplicate entry IDs, duplicated branch IDs, repeated memberships, conflicting declarations and dangling entries; resolves only unambiguous occurrence ownership without guessing.

dataclasses.asdict recursively copies collection fields and tracks new record fields without a parallel hand-maintained schema.

src/pubmed_search/domain/entities/pipeli.notes: Pure declarative DAG step carries params/dependencies/error policy; application validator enforces actions, IDs and cycle constraints.
Output shape contains format, positive-limit policy and ranking selection; validation remains centralized rather than duplicated in dataclass setters.
Separates custom steps, global variables and template inputs; factories provide independent mutable defaults.
Keeps article data/PMIDs, metadata and error distinct so partial pipeline execution remains inspectable.
Only None denotes absence of an error; even an empty-string error remains a failure signal.

Metadata envelope holds hashes/revision timestamps and counts independently from executable configuration.

Captures success/partial/error/timeout and set differences for scheduled search history without executing pipeline steps.
Persists current/new/removed PMIDs plus summary articles and timing/error data, preserving diff evidence.
Uses Python-3.10-compatible ISO parsing and legacy defaults for older stored run envelopes.
Schedule metadata is distinct from APScheduler runtime jobs; timezone and last error are persisted for reproducibility.

Fail-closed result separates parsed config from validation errors; callers check valid before execution.

Produces readable diagnostics from collected errors without trying to execute or repair invalid configurations.

src/pubmed_search/domain/entities/resear.notes: Recursive domain tree owns ordered events and children; builder produces acyclic branch topology rather than arbitrary graph references.
Sorts copies of events and child lists, avoiding in-place mutation of caller-owned list order.
Counts direct plus recursive descendant events, including branches without direct studies.
Returns a fresh chronological flattening of every descendant; downstream mutations of the list cannot change branch membership.
Uses known positive years across all descendant events and ignores undated records for date bounds.
Considers descendant events, so structural parent branches survive when only children contain studies.
Recursively preserves nonempty children while exporting direct events separately; avoids double-listing flattened events.
Top-level research grouping remains a projection model, with source totals and creation metadata independent of branch counts.
Aggregates branch totals without imposing global deduplication on legitimate branch memberships.
Preserves configured order while removing only recursively empty branches.
Combines valid child ranges and returns None for no dated evidence.
Exports active branches and their counts from the same selection; metadata remains a serialization view.
Replaced three duplicate event loops and corrupted box glyphs with one nested traversal; deeper branches and direct parent events are now retained.
Recurses through nonempty children before direct events, computes connectors across both groups and normalizes embedded title newlines; each event appears once.

src/pubmed_search/domain/entities/timeli.notes: Timeline-specific grammar normalization collapses line breaks and neutralizes HTML/directive delimiters; flowchart escaping is intentionally not reused across different Mermaid grammars.
Distinct trial, regulatory, synthesis and safety milestones preserve scientific meaning for scoring and branch classification.
Retained simplified evidence taxonomy with UNKNOWN; does not replace clinical judgment or infer evidence from citation count.
Frozen score record exposes component diagnostics independently from the overall weighted score selected by application scoring.
Descending thresholds cover boundaries and retain a standard category below the minimum notable score.
Uses the same thresholds as tier so display stars cannot disagree with the categorical score.
Rounds display components while retaining diagnostics; full-precision model values remain available for ranking.
Frozen outer event record preserves known date precision, citations, milestone confidence and optional scoring without retrieval logic.
Nonpositive years render Undated rather than fabricated dates; optional month is shown only when supplied by validated builders.
Undated events sort last, with month and PMID tie-breakers for deterministic chronology.
Serializes both machine milestone/evidence values and display date label, retaining metadata and optional landmark details.
Mutable collection groups event records with explicit boundaries; application builders determine meaningful periods.
Count is derived from current events so edits cannot leave a stale cached total.
Exports boundaries, description and full member records, preserving evidence details across grouping.
Aggregate remains mutable during construction; documentation no longer claims recursively immutable timeline collections.
Initial ordering sorts a copied list and retains unknown-date events at the end.
Derives total from the live events collection and includes undated evidence.
Only positive years contribute to range, preserving None when no dates are known.
Inclusive duration is zero for no known range and one for a single-year timeline.
Counts by stable enum wire values and includes all event types without ranking-based omission.
Exact enum matching returns a fresh subset, preserving source event order.
Exact year selection retains the explicit undated sentinel behavior rather than inventing an interval.
Inclusive bounds are explicit; reversed ranges produce an empty result without altering the aggregate.
An explicit score threshold takes precedence over citation count, and score zero is not mistaken for a missing threshold.
Exports the canonical timeline plus derived summaries/periods with ISO creation date; no network or rendering mutation.

src/pubmed_search/domain/services/articl.notes: Centralizes optional/single/list author normalization; filters unsupported members while retaining consortium strings and structured source names.
Null authors and malformed year fallback no longer abort mapping; specialized trial/review types precede generic Journal Article, and PMC provenance still supplies the OA link.
Empty titles/null dates or authors are tolerated; zero citations survive, and unverified PDF/TDM links remain raw provenance instead of false OA declarations.
Uses root-level inverted-index positions rather than provider-specific nested assumptions, skipping malformed containers and sorting words deterministically.
Normalizes documented PMC URL and numeric provider forms; strict untrusted user validation remains in the separate identifier value object.
Reviewed nullable locations, identifiers, abstract index and source-type mapping; citation zero now creates a metric record instead of disappearing.
Maps external IDs and optional PDF/license metadata, infers preprint only without PubMed/journal evidence and preserves zero citation counts.
Uses normalized CORE contract and common author parser; retains download/PDF/reader preference, source ID and explicit zero citation metrics.
Merged identical Scopus/WoS bibliographic mapping while preserving caller-supplied source attribution and OA flag requirements.
Thin named adapter keeps the public source entrypoint and delegates only the shared normalized payload shape.
Thin named adapter preserves WoS source tracking independently of Scopus while sharing identical mapping logic.
Copies the payload before adapting PMC/journal aliases, reuses PubMed normalization and replaces provenance with Europe PMC attribution.
Preserves preprint type/version and server attribution, parses date precision without fetching, and uses the shared author parser for nullable payloads.

src/pubmed_search/domain/value_objects/a.notes: Typed ValueError allows public tools to distinguish malformed identifiers from upstream transport failures.
Frozen/slotted parsed identifier holds kind/value; factory validation remains the intended construction boundary.
Rejects wrong types, blank/control-bearing and oversized text before individual grammar parsing.
Rejects booleans, signs, lookalike digits and arbitrary prose while allowing the documented integer/prefix forms.
Catches only the deliberate validation exception, preserving unrelated programmer failures for diagnosis.
Normalizes numeric/PMC/PMCID forms without stripping arbitrary characters; false values cannot become article IDs.
Returns None only on identifier validation failures and delegates all normalization to the strict parser.
Retains ordered deduplication, batch length bounds and exclusive last sentinel; recursive list support is existing Python compatibility, while MCP schema constrains nesting.
Dispatches by full prefixes and validates the whole input; never extracts an apparently valid substring from prose.

src/pubmed_search/domain/value_objects/i.notes: Distinct validation failure prevents confusing an invalid terminology code with a provider miss.
Frozen value includes the detected code system so ambiguous code strings cannot silently select an ontology.
Checks entire bounded ASCII grammar, rejects cross-version ambiguity, and does not claim syntactic validity proves current codebook membership.

src/pubmed_search/domain/value_objects/n.notes: Typed numeric-database validation error is separate from PubMed/DOI and source failures.
Requires positive ASCII digit strings with a bounded length; no coercion of floats/booleans or surrounding prose into different records.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/__i.notes: Lazy exports load only requested modules, preserve public names and raise AttributeError for unknown names without initializing clients.
Combines real globals and declared lazy exports for introspection; no service construction occurs during discovery.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/age.notes: Rejects nonpositive/bool repeats; requires complete arm/query/repeat pairs and averages repeats per held-out query before comparison.
Normalizes acceptable answer aliases and reports exact/token overlap separately; does not claim entailment or citation validity.
Case folding, punctuation and whitespace normalization apply identically to expected and produced answers.
Deduplicates retrieved identities, requires selected records to have been observed and separates retrieval from selection metrics.
Rejects nonfinite scores, pairs the same query IDs and uses deterministic seeded bootstrap over paired differences.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/cli.notes: Closed purpose enum limits the licensed citation adapter contract without adding an autonomous research workflow.
Application request separates question, permitted purpose and end-user context; provider credentials stay outside the model.
Allowlisted bibliographic fields exclude generated clinical advice and raw licensed content from the response contract.
Ephemeral citation batch carries attribution and diagnostics, distinct from persistable UnifiedArticle search results.
Narrow injected port keeps licensed provider access out of presentation and domain models.
Async contract returns an ephemeral batch; governance and entitlement checks remain with the implementing adapter.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/icd.notes: Delegates whole-input grammar to the strict value object; ambiguous/invalid codes remain explicit failures.
Looks up the bounded curated crosswalk, retains parent-code fallback and identifies mapping scope without claiming complete ontology coverage.
Searches only curated mappings and returns matching codes with their versions; no terminology service or clinical coding inference is implied.
Returns curated categories/reference metadata rather than claiming authoritative membership validation.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/pic.notes: Distinct ValueError preserves user-correctable handoff failures separately from retrieval errors.
Rejects nonstring, oversized and NUL-bearing fields before YAML construction; optional None becomes an empty element.
Retained as advisory fallback only when omitted; explicit caller question type overrides heuristic clinical keyword matching.
JSON string quoting safely produces YAML scalar text with literal newlines/quotes escaped rather than interpolated as structure.
Emits the established pico template contract and includes separate search expressions only when different from descriptive elements.
Requires population/intervention, treats comparator as optional and outcome as recommended; no automatic clinical claim generation.
Bounds all fields, sources/profile/result budgets and hands an explicit inspectable plan to the pipeline instead of executing it.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/que.notes: Stable sorted whole-word English matching avoids substring operators such as or in corticosteroid; CJK phrases retain substring detection.
Distinct simple/moderate/complex/ambiguous categories serve planning hints, not measured difficulty scores.
Separates lookup, systematic and citation-tracking intentions so identifiers do not erase requested relationship retrieval.
Optional heuristic slots remain separate from the explicitly validated agent PICO handoff.
Population and intervention define this heuristic's completeness; does not imply clinically sufficient review design.
Only populated comparator qualifies; empty strings do not force comparative planning.
Serializes known slots without substituting inferred evidence or modifying the object.
Carries recognized namespace and source text so downstream lookup need not re-guess the identifier type.
Planning DTO keeps original/normalized query, identifiers, constraints and advisory diagnostics together.
Converts enum and optional PICO values into the existing wire view while preserving confidence as a heuristic.
Stateless analysis service keeps deterministic extraction independent of network providers; removed empty constructor.
Coordinates normalization and namespace/year extraction before intent, complexity and strategy hints; no source I/O occurs here.

Whole-word signals and explicit systematic/citation intent precede broad comparison/lookup fallbacks.
Drops field/operator syntax while preserving short biomedical tokens and alphanumeric names such as RA and IL-6.
Retained explicitly as heuristic extraction for planning; authoritative structured PICO fields come from pico_plan validation.

Returns recommendations from intent/complexity only; enabled source registry and explicit exclusions govern actual dispatch.

Word-boundary image/anatomy hints avoid unrelated substring hits; remains an advisory signal rather than automatic image retrieval.
Retains bounded rule-based confidence and missing-information penalties; not presented as calibrated probability.
One known-tag recognizer shared by planning and fallback prevents dialect rules diverging between retrieval routes.
Keeps original errors/warnings and optional suggestions separate; suggested corrections are not automatically executed.
Checks collected warnings without conflating them with invalid syntax or provider failures.
Builds user diagnostics from validation findings and proposed correction, preserving the original query.
Local syntax lint service checks common errors without claiming to implement the complete PubMed grammar.
Combines parenthesis, quote, tag and operator findings; a generated correction remains explicitly advisory.
Tracks quoted text so literal delimiters do not affect grouping balance; reports unmatched boundaries.
Identifies unmatched delimiters and supported smart-quote normalization without issuing searches.
Known tags remain accepted and near-match suggestions are now sorted deterministically.
Flags common operator placement/casing errors while leaving complex interpretation to the provider.
Best-effort suggestion only; callers do not silently execute repaired grouping as equivalent semantics.
Completes common quote mistakes in a suggestion, not an automatic source request rewrite.
Retained as an explicit proposed edit because operator repair may change search semantics.
Bounds edit-distance suggestions and avoids recommending unrelated field names as valid syntax.
Dynamic-programming edit distance uses bounded known field names; retains deterministic insertion/deletion/substitution costs.
Convenience facade delegates to the same validator, avoiding a second public validation implementation.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/ran.notes: Shared biomedical tokenizer preserves short/alphanumeric meaningful terms for corpus and fallback scoring.
Removes PubMed field and Boolean syntax before applying the same text tokenization as article documents.
Stores corpus frequencies/lengths independently of article entity mutation and provider retrieval.
Builds document frequencies from per-document unique terms while lengths retain actual token counts.
Combines bibliographic text/keywords in the intended relevance fields; missing text contributes no fabricated tokens.
Uses corpus statistics with guarded empty documents/query and term frequency saturation; retrieval order is not a semantic score.
Normalizes scores for a supplied batch without claiming cross-query calibration; zero-score cases remain finite.
Keeps fused articles, scores and per-dimension contributions separate for inspectable ranking output.
Deduplicates votes per ranker, gives absent documents zero credit and rejects nonfinite parameters; caller bypasses canonical collisions.
Returns selected articles alongside lexical diversity diagnostics; no embedding similarity is claimed.
Validates finite weights/scores and nonnegative limits, handles top_k zero and uses indexed fallback relevance to avoid duplicate-object lookup errors.
Describes source-set overlap rather than provider rank disagreement or research-topic maturity.
Rounds diagnostics only in the serialized view, retaining raw precision in the record.

Uses the shared canonical identity policy for ranking interoperability; aggregation separately guards conflicting strong IDs.
Empty-set behavior is explicit and intersection/union score stays bounded for lexical term sets.
Handles fewer than two documents and averages each unordered pair once.

Threshold label derives from the heuristic composite and does not certify measured rerun agreement.
Combines declared heuristic components and weights; source overlap is based on actual queried/responded sets.
Syntax features supply a documented heuristic, not a guarantee that formal queries retrieve relevant studies.
Unique responded intersection divided by unique queried sources; duplicates and unsolicited sources earn no extra credit, no-query retains unknown prior.
Retains source-specific prior estimates as heuristic metadata; no comparison against a second retrieval is performed.
Scores available trace fields, not correctness or clinical evidentiary strength of the trace.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/res.notes: Retained lazy import used by ranking; removed unrelated dead entity-import cache rather than changing public imports.

Finite ranking dimensions match serialized contributions and configurable weighting fields.
Strict identifiers, standard title fallback and aggressive matching remain explicit caller choices.

Constructs the established impact-priority weights without making citation count a relevance judgment.
Constructs explicit recency weights; date decay policy remains independently configurable.
Retains publication-type proxy weights, described as indicators rather than verified study quality.
Keeps matched-entity relevance emphasis independently configurable from citation impact.
Rejects negative/nonfinite values and preserves an all-zero configuration without division failure.
Looks up the configured publication-type proxy and supplies the documented unknown-type fallback.
Counts retrieved/deduplicated records and source contributions without conflating them with provider total matches.
Exports counts and optional diagnostic data from the completed aggregation, not guessed provider totals.
Single disjoint-set implementation supports transitive duplicate grouping with caller-owned compatibility checks.
Creates independent parent/rank arrays for the exact candidate count.
Path compression preserves component roots while reducing repeated traversal cost.

Enumerates every index exactly once after final root compression, including singleton components.
Application-owned deterministic dedup/ranking service has no provider I/O or presentation formatting responsibility.
Retains caller configuration and initializes no clients or network state.
Flattens source batches, records source counts and delegates one unified deduplication pass.
Excludes zero-weight dimensions from fusion, retains canonical collisions via local row scoring and consolidates weighted fallback loops.

Applies per-call dedup and ranking policy together via an isolated aggregator; max_results zero is respected and negative limits rejected.
Every namespace contributes identity evidence; component-level conflicts block transitive merges and title-only groups cannot invent identifier propagation.
Checks all shared namespaces before merging roots and combines component identity sets only after compatibility succeeds.
All recognized identifier namespaces disqualify ambiguous title-only matching.
Selects the most complete/trusted record deterministically before filling missing metadata.
Counts identifiers and metadata separately, then applies source trust as a stable final tie-breaker.
Computes the declared dimensions from one configuration and accepts precomputed corpus relevance to avoid inconsistent scoring.
Uses the shared query/text tokenization and explicit title/abstract/keyword weighting; no substring relevance matching.
Publication type, metadata and OA are bounded proxies; score does not assert methodological or clinical quality.
Rejects invalid half-life and caps future publication age at zero; absent year retains a documented low-neutral prior.
Rejects invalid/negative/nonfinite provider metrics, caps percentile and avoids zero-division from malformed negative RCR.
Normalizes only finite nonnegative numeric values and rejects booleans as bibliometric measurements.
Uses configured source priors plus corroboration and bounds the score; multiple providers do not prove evidence correctness.
Whole-word escaped matching prevents short entity names matching inside unrelated terms; empty hints retain a neutral score.
Delegates tolerant matching normalization to the shared identity helper instead of duplicating strict user-input parsing.
Normalizes comparison text consistently; minimum length and strong-ID restrictions are enforced before title deduplication.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/ret.notes: Deduplicates ranked IDs, bounds depth and computes recall/precision/MRR and graded nDCG against supplied judgments; unjudged retrieved items receive zero gain.

Explicitly PubMed syntax for MeSH/gene/literal terms; provider-neutral conversion remains with the unified planner.

None represents a valid unresolved term; resolver errors are handled by enhancement fallback.

Preserves term provenance and heuristic confidence separately from the source query expression.

Orders strategies by descending intended priority through the existing sort contract.
Collects resolved entities, expansion variants and metadata without executing searches.

Returns actual available MeSH IDs and excludes unresolved entities.
Returns None for no strategies and the maximum-priority plan otherwise.
Serializes relevant entity/term/strategy provenance without raw upstream payloads or private cache keys.

Injected resolver/cache retain application boundaries and explicit empty caches are preserved.

Uses opaque tenant-scoped cache keys, distinguishes None and caches only successful entity resolutions.
Excludes field tags/operators, retains quoted phrases and short biomedical names, and deduplicates case-insensitively in stable order.
Keeps original retrieval and provider-neutral alternatives, adds valid optional variants and omits empty broad queries.

Retains original PubMed and Europe PMC variants without resolver dependence or fabricated resolved entities.

src/pubmed_search/application/search/sou.notes: Explicit open/licensed enum separates contract eligibility from technical reachability.
Distinguishes standard persistence from ephemeral metadata without introducing hidden retention defaults.
One shared operation vocabulary covers dispatch, storage/export and registration so adapters can fail closed consistently.
PermissionError subtype preserves policy failures separately from provider transport errors.

Exact operation membership check does not infer permission from related allowed operations.
Fails before forbidden operations with provider and operation identifiers but no raw question or credentials.
Typed page preserves articles, optional total and diagnostics; absence of a provider total is not substituted with page length.
Constructs a valid empty page without inventing a known total or upstream failure.
Accepts nonnegative integer/ASCII decimal totals only and emits sanitized diagnostics without raw provider values.

src/pubmed_search/application/unified/cl.notes: Contract violations remain distinct from transport failures and do not become valid empty retrievals.
Rendering failure preserves successful retrieval provenance instead of reporting the entire adjunct as absent.
Mutable handoff separates retrieval and rendering state, counts and sanitized error metadata.
Initializes pending states only for an explicitly requested adjunct and disables rendering state for JSON output.
Format failure has precedence; pending Markdown remains pending after retrieval rather than prematurely complete.
Requires valid complete/empty retrieval and completed or inapplicable formatting.
Preserves zero as a valid empty outcome and bypasses unnecessary formatting when no rows exist.
Normalizes errors without raw exception text and deduplicates user warnings.
Malformed provider rows become a nonretryable validation failure with a fixed safe message.
Marks formatting complete only after nonempty successful retrieval.
Retains result count while recording a sanitized projection error separately from retrieval.
Versioned coverage exports known-safe error fields and copies warnings rather than leaking raw exceptions.
Reuses shared error normalization and accepts only bounded nonbool HTTP codes from provider wrappers.
Projects sanitized source errors including retryability/status without duplicating exception parsing.
Checks list/record contracts, required fields and exact ASCII NCT identifiers before exposing adjunct data.

src/pubmed_search/application/unified/ex.notes: Uses stable identity tie-breaking around application ranking, keeping final enrichment candidate order reproducible locally.
Carries articles, source outcomes and optional adjunct/depth diagnostics across the use-case boundary.
Serializes the shared sanitized error contract rather than arbitrary provider exception strings.
Distinguishes typed page, valid zero result and contract violation; attaches source-specific diagnostics without fabricating totals.
Preserves partial primary results, explicit/systematic source constraints and finally cancels adjunct work even when foreground progress raises.
Retrieves late task failures without logging raw content and ignores properly cancelled tasks.
Captures source/function arguments per invocation and builds source-isolated awaitables.
Normalizes one source result inside the concurrency/error collection boundary.
